pathway.title: Ati Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is falling because earnings are rising, not because debt is being repaid. Total debt over reported EBITDA fell from 2.54x at FY2024 to 2.22x at FY2025 and 1.92x on the last twelve months, but net debt rose from USD 1,332.7 million at FY2025 to USD 1,415.2 million at 2026-09-27, so the gain came from last-twelve-months reported EBITDA reaching USD 968.5 million, not from paydown. On FY2025 EBITDA of USD 789.0 million the same debt would be 2.35x total and 1.79x net, and on the lower FY2024 EBITDA of USD 745.8 million it would be 2.49x and 1.90x, so the ratios depend on the earnings step-up holding. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8

Liquidity and maturities are the strongest part of the credit. Liquidity of USD 1,012.3 million, made of USD 442.3 million of cash and about USD 570 million of undrawn revolving capacity, covers the next senior note maturity of USD 325.0 million, due in the fourth quarter of FY2029, 3.11 times, and the 2026 refinancing replaced the USD 350.0 million of 2027 notes with USD 450.0 million of unsecured 2033 notes. The only maturity ladder printed predates that refinancing and shows FY2030 as the largest year at USD 633.4 million, consistent with the 2030 notes and the asset-based term loan falling due together, so the test of market access sits in FY2029 and FY2030, not before. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C1

Free cash flow is real but is being fully distributed. Free cash flow was USD 333.7 million in FY2025 and USD 198.0 million in 9M 2026, USD 421.1 million over the last twelve months or 43.48% of reported EBITDA, after inventories absorbed USD 255.1 million and capital expenditures were USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026. Shareholder returns of USD 277.2 million in the same nine months exceeded free cash flow by USD 79.2 million, and treasury stock purchases were 140.85% of free cash flow in FY2025, so cash that could have repaid debt went to holders and net debt rose. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10

Revenue visibility is good for about a year and improving. Confirmed orders were about USD 4.3 billion at 2026-09-27 against about USD 3.6 billion a year earlier, and about 75% of them are due to be satisfied within the next 12 months; most major engine and airframe makers hold long-term agreements with the company, and no customer exceeded 10% of sales. This supersedes the year-end reading in Business & governance that orders fell from about USD 3.9 billion to about USD 3.7 billion, because the interim figure is later and shows growth over the year, although the backlog eased slightly from about USD 4.4 billion at 2026-06-28. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-06-28_ati_ati-20260628.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Business risk rests on one cycle. Aerospace and defense was about 68% of FY2025 sales and commercial jet engines alone were 42% of Q3 2026 sales, and commercial jet engines were 74% of the engine-component segment's Q3 2026 sales; the annual report calls the commercial aerospace cycle hard to predict, so a fall in engine build rates would reach revenue, margin and cash flow together, and other markets at 31% of Q3 2026 sales soften that only partly. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 40

Margins are improving on volume, price and mix, but the gain is concentrated in one segment and exposed to input costs. The issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% in Q3 2026 against 20.0% a year earlier, and Advanced Alloys & Solutions earned segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million against USD 90.4 million, a margin of 25.8% against 17.3%, while the High Performance Materials & Components margin eased to 23.2% from 24.2% on the cost of moving a new superalloy into production. Raw material surcharges pass most nickel and titanium moves through, but hedges cover only about 7% of a year's nickel purchases, so tariffs and delays can hit margin before recovery. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 17

Funding outside reported debt flatters leverage. Supplier financing of USD 83.0 million and USD 120 million used under the receivables facility total USD 203.0 million, 14.34% of net debt, and customers' receivable programmes took USD 377.5 million of invoices in 9M 2026. If banks or customers withdrew these programmes, working capital would absorb cash and net leverage would be higher than reported. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C14

Financial policy is the weakest dimension. The company pays no dividend but has USD 425 million of repurchase authority left, the asset-based facility sets no dividend limit while undrawn availability stays above the greater of USD 120 million and 20% of the facility, and the nearest senior note maturity is far enough away that buybacks can continue without an immediate refinancing constraint. Holders above reporting thresholds are not established, so no controlling owner is identified to weigh either way; the 60%-owned Chinese joint venture holds USD 106.1 million of the cash, which is not wholly available to creditors of the parent. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

cells.text: ATI Inc. produces specialty materials and components, mainly nickel-based alloys and superalloys, titanium and titanium-based alloys, and zirconium, hafnium and niobium products, in two segments: High Performance Materials & Components (HPMC) and Advanced Alloys & Solutions (AA&S)
Qualified, hard-to-replace products give pricing power but tie the credit to a few industrial cycles
HPMC was 53% and AA&S 47% of FY2025 revenue (HPMC 2,441.7 and AA&S 2,145.7 of 4,587.4 external sales); the split was 52% and 48% in FY2024
Two segments of similar size; HPMC carries the engine-component growth and the higher margin
Aerospace and defense was about 68% of FY2025 sales and 69% of Q3 2026 sales; commercial jet engines were 42% of Q3 2026 sales, airframes 15% and defense 12%
A single end-market cycle drives most revenue and cash flow
About 92% of HPMC revenue is aerospace and defense, including nearly 68% from commercial jet engine products; defense is nearly 11% of HPMC sales
HPMC earnings follow engine build rates and spare-parts demand
Aerospace and defense is about 41% of AA&S revenue in FY2025 and 45% in Q3 2026; the rest is energy, automotive, electronics, medical and other industrial markets
More cyclical industrial exposure than HPMC but diversifying; mix is moving toward aerospace

Long-term agreements with most major aerospace engine and airframe makers; a substantial part of HPMC products is sold under multi-year agreements; no single customer accounted for more than 10% of sales in any year presented
Contract cover gives volume visibility, though renewal and re-pricing risk is stated
Confirmed orders were about 3.7 billion at 2025-12-28 against about 3.9 billion at 2024-12-29, of which about 70% is expected to ship in FY2026; HPMC about 3.1 billion and AA&S about 0.6 billion
A year of shipments is covered, but backlog fell year on year while sales grew
International sales were about 42% of FY2025 sales and direct exports from US operations about 34%; international sales were 37% of 9M 2026 sales against 42% a year earlier
Tariff and trade-policy exposure on exports and imported nickel and titanium inputs

Nickel, titanium sponge, zirconium and hafnium are sourced from several countries; most products are sold under contracts with raw material surcharges and index mechanisms; nickel hedges cover about 5 million pounds, about 7% of a year's purchases
Surcharges pass most metal-price moves through; an unhedged gap remains on delay and tariffs
About 7,600 employees; about 35% are covered by collective agreements; agreements reached on 2025-04-22 for about 1,100 AA&S employees run to 2031-02-28
Labour terms are fixed for the AA&S plants to 2031, limiting strike risk there
Modest weakness in the third quarter, mostly from planned late-summer outages by European aerospace customers
A single quarter can understate the run rate

runs.text: The first strength is the earnings-led fall in leverage: last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 968.5 million puts total debt at 1.92x and net debt at 1.46x, so interest cover and refinancing capacity improve for as long as earnings hold, and the issuer's own ratios of 1.74x and 1.33x on Adjusted EBITDA point the same way. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

The second strength is the liquidity and maturity runway: USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity covers the next senior note maturity of USD 325.0 million 3.11 times, so no refinancing is needed before FY2029 and the company can fund working capital and capacity growth from cash and the revolver. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

The third strength is contract cover: long-term agreements with most major aerospace makers, no customer above 10% of sales and orders of about USD 4.3 billion, about 75% of them due within the next 12 months, fix volume for about a year and steady the cash flow that services debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The first weakness is shareholder returns above free cash flow: USD 277.2 million of returns against USD 198.0 million of free cash flow in 9M 2026, leave a gap of USD 79.2 million, so net debt rises even as EBITDA grows and leverage falls only if earnings keep rising. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; calculation C10

The second weakness is concentration in one cycle: about 68% of FY2025 sales are aerospace and defense, so a downturn in engine build rates would cut EBITDA and lift leverage together, and the company's own statement that the cycle is hard to predict leaves no basis for assuming it away. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The third weakness is funding outside reported debt: supplier financing and receivables facility funding of USD 203.0 million equal 14.34% of net debt and could reverse, which would raise net leverage above the reported 1.46x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C14

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-06-03 ATI Inc. issued USD 450 million of senior notes due 2033, unsecured and unsubordinated, with net proceeds of USD 443.1 million after USD 6.9 million of fees, and on 2026-07-08 it used about USD 350 million of the proceeds to redeem the senior notes due 2027 in full, recording a debt extinguishment charge of USD 1.2 million. The refinancing added no secured debt and moved the next maturity to the fourth quarter of FY2029. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 47

The asset-based credit facility was amended on 2025-06-13 and now runs to June 2030, with a USD 600 million revolver, a USD 200 million term loan and a letter of credit sub-limit of USD 200 million; USD 29.3 million of letters of credit were used and nothing was drawn on the revolver at 2026-09-27. A receivables facility of up to USD 125.0 million, entered on 2025-09-19, had USD 120 million of funding used at 2026-09-27; receivables sold under it leave the balance sheet and so sit outside reported debt. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

No acquisition is described in the filings for FY2024 to 9M 2026. The transactions that moved cash were debt repayment and refinancing, small disposals and share repurchases, with USD 425 million of repurchase authority remaining at 2026-09-27. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_ati_ati-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-27_ati_ati-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

fields.value: The strongest case against the benign reading is that it rests on a sharp earnings step-up: the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% in Q3 2026 against 20.0% in Q3 2025, and the AA&S segment's EBITDA of USD 181.3 million in Q3 2026 was about double the USD 90.4 million of a year earlier, so the trailing denominator contains an unusually strong quarter. The view would weaken if net debt keeps rising while reported EBITDA stalls, if inventory build is not matched by shipments, or if the USD 425 million repurchase authorisation is funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if cash interest for the nine months is disclosed and confirms cover near the annual level, or if shareholder returns fall back within free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ati Inc is a technically qualified but end-market-concentrated aerospace and defense materials supplier, with large-holder ownership not established and buybacks as the main way cash leaves the company, so creditors depend on engine demand and board restraint on payouts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is concentrated in aerospace and defense but backed by contracts. The sector was about 68% of FY2025 sales and 69% of Q3 2026 sales, with commercial jet engines at 42% of Q3 2026 sales; about 92% of High Performance Materials & Components revenue and 41% of Advanced Alloys & Solutions revenue come from it. Most major engine and airframe makers have long-term agreements with the company, no customer exceeded 10% of sales, and confirmed orders were about USD 3.7 billion at 2025-12-28, of which about 70% were due to ship in FY2026. For creditors that means a year of covered volume against a cycle the company itself calls hard to predict.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth is strong and driven by volume and pricing, which supports near-term cash flow, but one segment's quarterly margin eased. Sales rose 26.49% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and 12.49% over 9M 2026; Advanced Alloys & Solutions earned segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million against USD 90.4 million, while High Performance Materials & Components earned USD 167.3 million against USD 145.8 million and its quarterly margin eased to 23.2% from 24.2% on the cost of moving a new nickel-based superalloy into production, although its nine-month margin rose to 24.0% from 23.4%. That cost is the main operating item to watch because the engine-component segment carries most of the growth case.

fields.value: Ownership does not read as a sponsor story, but it is not established. The company has a broad record-holder base, pays no dividend, and the filings read name no controlling or large holder; holdings above reporting thresholds, board composition and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The only named outside owner is China Baowu Steel Group with 40% of the Chinese strip joint venture, whose cash and dividends belong partly to that minority. The consequence is no evidence of sponsor extraction or support in either direction, and payout risk comes from the board and public holders rather than a financial owner.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is mixed: debt is refinanced early and lengthened, but cash goes to buybacks faster than it is generated. In 2026 the company issued USD 450.0 million of 2033 notes and redeemed USD 350.0 million of 2027 notes ahead of maturity, which removes the nearest maturity, yet treasury stock purchases were USD 470.0 million in FY2025, 140.85% of free cash flow of USD 333.7 million, and USD 195.0 million in 9M 2026, 98.48% of free cash flow. The credit facility sets no limit on dividends while undrawn availability stays above the greater of USD 120 million and 20% of the facility, and the filings do not say whether repurchases face the same test, so creditor protection rests on that availability and on board policy.

fields.value: Capital spending is rising to fund aerospace growth, and it competes with debt reduction for cash. Capital expenditures were USD 239.1 million in FY2024, USD 280.6 million in FY2025 and USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026 against USD 187.9 million in 9M 2025, mainly growth projects, and restructuring and transformation charges recur. Free cash flow after this spending, not EBITDA, is what is available for debt reduction.

fields.value: Claims outside debt are modest against earnings but not zero. Pension and retiree benefit liabilities were USD 187.9 million at 2026-09-27, environmental reserves are about USD 15 million with up to USD 21 million more reasonably possible, and a pension class action over the 2023 annuity purchase is pending with a recommendation to dismiss. These claims sit outside reported debt and would matter mainly in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a stable reading is concentration and cyclicality: the company says commercial aerospace has been cyclical and hard to predict, confirmed orders fell to about USD 3.7 billion from about USD 3.9 billion while sales rose, about 35% of the workforce is under collective agreements, international sales were about 42% of FY2025 sales and nickel hedges cover only about 7% of a year's purchases, so trade policy and metal prices can hit margins faster than surcharges recover them. Buybacks that exceed free cash flow add to this by keeping net debt from falling when earnings are strong. The view would weaken if engine build rates or the order backlog fall, if the quarterly margin of the engine-component segment keeps easing, or if buybacks are funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if the proxy statement shows no dominant holder with payout influence, or if the board caps payouts at free cash flow.

fields.value: Ati Inc's credit profile is improving, with total debt at 1.92x and net debt at 1.46x reported EBITDA and USD 1,012.3 million of liquidity, so near-term refinancing risk is low, but shareholder returns exceed free cash flow, so deleveraging relies on earnings.

fields.value: Leverage is falling because earnings are rising, not because debt is being repaid. Total debt over reported EBITDA fell from 2.54x at FY2024 to 2.22x at FY2025 and 1.92x on the last twelve months, but net debt rose from USD 1,332.7 million at FY2025 to USD 1,415.2 million at 2026-09-27, so the gain came from last-twelve-months reported EBITDA reaching USD 968.5 million, not from paydown. On FY2025 EBITDA of USD 789.0 million the same debt would be 2.35x total and 1.79x net, and on the lower FY2024 EBITDA of USD 745.8 million it would be 2.49x and 1.90x, so the ratios depend on the earnings step-up holding.

fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are the strongest part of the credit. Liquidity of USD 1,012.3 million, made of USD 442.3 million of cash and about USD 570 million of undrawn revolving capacity, covers the next senior note maturity of USD 325.0 million, due in the fourth quarter of FY2029, 3.11 times, and the 2026 refinancing replaced the USD 350.0 million of 2027 notes with USD 450.0 million of unsecured 2033 notes. The only maturity ladder printed predates that refinancing and shows FY2030 as the largest year at USD 633.4 million, consistent with the 2030 notes and the asset-based term loan falling due together, so the test of market access sits in FY2029 and FY2030, not before.

fields.value: Free cash flow is real but is being fully distributed. Free cash flow was USD 333.7 million in FY2025 and USD 198.0 million in 9M 2026, USD 421.1 million over the last twelve months or 43.48% of reported EBITDA, after inventories absorbed USD 255.1 million and capital expenditures were USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026. Shareholder returns of USD 277.2 million in the same nine months exceeded free cash flow by USD 79.2 million, and treasury stock purchases were 140.85% of free cash flow in FY2025, so cash that could have repaid debt went to holders and net debt rose.

fields.value: Revenue visibility is good for about a year and improving. Confirmed orders were about USD 4.3 billion at 2026-09-27 against about USD 3.6 billion a year earlier, and about 75% of them are due to be satisfied within the next 12 months; most major engine and airframe makers hold long-term agreements with the company, and no customer exceeded 10% of sales. This supersedes the year-end reading in Business & governance that orders fell from about USD 3.9 billion to about USD 3.7 billion, because the interim figure is later and shows growth over the year, although the backlog eased slightly from about USD 4.4 billion at 2026-06-28.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk rests on one cycle. Aerospace and defense was about 68% of FY2025 sales and commercial jet engines alone were 42% of Q3 2026 sales, and commercial jet engines were 74% of the engine-component segment's Q3 2026 sales; the annual report calls the commercial aerospace cycle hard to predict, so a fall in engine build rates would reach revenue, margin and cash flow together, and other markets at 31% of Q3 2026 sales soften that only partly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are improving on volume, price and mix, but the gain is concentrated in one segment and exposed to input costs. The issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% in Q3 2026 against 20.0% a year earlier, and Advanced Alloys & Solutions earned segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million against USD 90.4 million, a margin of 25.8% against 17.3%, while the High Performance Materials & Components margin eased to 23.2% from 24.2% on the cost of moving a new superalloy into production. Raw material surcharges pass most nickel and titanium moves through, but hedges cover only about 7% of a year's nickel purchases, so tariffs and delays can hit margin before recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Funding outside reported debt flatters leverage. Supplier financing of USD 83.0 million and USD 120 million used under the receivables facility total USD 203.0 million, 14.34% of net debt, and customers' receivable programmes took USD 377.5 million of invoices in 9M 2026. If banks or customers withdrew these programmes, working capital would absorb cash and net leverage would be higher than reported.

fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension. The company pays no dividend but has USD 425 million of repurchase authority left, the asset-based facility sets no dividend limit while undrawn availability stays above the greater of USD 120 million and 20% of the facility, and the nearest senior note maturity is far enough away that buybacks can continue without an immediate refinancing constraint. Holders above reporting thresholds are not established, so no controlling owner is identified to weigh either way; the 60%-owned Chinese joint venture holds USD 106.1 million of the cash, which is not wholly available to creditors of the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an improving reading is that the fall in leverage rests on one earnings step-up concentrated in one quarter and one segment: Advanced Alloys & Solutions segment EBITDA of USD 181.3 million in Q3 2026 was about double the USD 90.4 million of a year earlier, net debt did not fall, and shareholder returns exceeded free cash flow. If earnings fell back to the FY2025 level with debt unchanged, total debt over reported EBITDA would be 2.35x and net debt 1.79x, above the 1.92x and 1.46x reported now, and 2.49x and 1.90x at the FY2024 level. Revenue growth of 9.29% over FY2025 produced EBITDA growth of 22.75%, so operating leverage works in both directions. The evidence for the view is that backlog is above its level of a year earlier and liquidity covers the next maturity 3.11 times, so a fall to the FY2025 or FY2024 earnings level would raise leverage but not threaten liquidity. The view would weaken if confirmed orders fall below USD 4.3 billion, if the engine-component margin keeps easing, if free cash flow stays below shareholder returns, or if buybacks are funded from the revolving facility. It would strengthen if free cash flow covers shareholder returns and net debt starts to fall while EBITDA holds.

fields.value: ATI Inc. makes specialty materials and components, mainly nickel-based alloys and superalloys, titanium alloys and zirconium, hafnium and niobium products, in two segments of similar size: High Performance Materials & Components, which sells engine and airframe parts mostly under multi-year agreements, and Advanced Alloys & Solutions, which sells flat-rolled products into aerospace, energy, automotive and electronics markets. Qualified products and long-term agreements support visibility of cash flow, so debt service capacity is good while the cycle holds; the concentration in commercial aerospace means a cyclical decline would reach both segments, and the year of covered orders limits how fast it would show in cash flow and liquidity.

fields.value: The common stock is listed and widely held, no controlling or large holder is named in the filings read, and holders above reporting thresholds, board composition and related-party dealings are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied. The only named outside owner is China Baowu Steel Group with 40% of the Chinese strip joint venture, which the company controls with 60% and consolidates, and that joint venture's USD 106.1 million of cash sits inside consolidated cash. The issuer is ATI Inc. itself; guarantors of the notes are not stated. The credit consequence is no evidence of sponsor extraction or support, with payout behaviour set by the board's repurchase decisions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, concentrated by end market but not by customer, and covered by contracts for about a year. Volume, price and mix drove growth of 26.49% in Q3 2026, led by commercial jet engine products, and about 75% of the USD 4.3 billion backlog is due within the next 12 months. Most products are sold under contracts with raw material surcharges and index mechanisms, which pass metal prices through, but the annual report states that long-term contracts can be renegotiated or re-priced at intervals and that excess capacity and competition have at times cut prices excluding surcharges. The credit implication is predictable revenue in the near term with re-pricing risk at renewals and cyclical risk beyond the order book.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a build-rate shock combined with input cost inflation. Last-twelve-months revenue grew 9.29% over FY2025 while reported EBITDA grew 22.75%, which shows strong operating leverage on the way up and the same leverage on the way down. About 35% of the workforce is covered by collective bargaining agreements, nickel hedges cover only about 7% of a year's purchases, and the engine-component segment margin eased in Q3 2026 on superalloy ramp costs, so fixed labour and ramp costs could outrun surcharges in a downturn; the split of fixed and variable costs is not stated.

fields.value: Free cash flow conversion is moderate and absorbs growth investment, so EBITDA does not translate fully into cash for debt service. Free cash flow was 42.29% of reported EBITDA in FY2025 and 25.44% in 9M 2026, when inventories took USD 255.1 million, and 43.48% over the last twelve months. Capital expenditures were USD 239.1 million in FY2024, USD 280.6 million in FY2025 and USD 216.6 million in 9M 2026, mainly growth projects the company can slow, so capex is flexible; interest and commitment fees paid were USD 117.8 million in FY2025, and the split of maintenance and growth capex is not stated. The implication is that debt reduction depends on free cash flow after returns, which was negative in 9M 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate in qualified aerospace products and higher in flat-rolled industrial products. The annual report names Precision Castparts under Berkshire Hathaway, Howmet Aerospace, Carpenter Technology and Aubert & Duval as principal competitors of the engine-component segment, and Haynes International and VDM Metals for nickel-based alloys in the alloy segment; market shares are not stated, and the filing says competition and excess capacity have at times reduced prices excluding surcharges. Rivalry therefore caps pricing power in industrial markets but is less of a threat to margin in qualified aerospace products.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low in aerospace because fulfilling contracts requires meeting exacting performance requirements and product specifications, and the company's melt, forging, finishing and machining integration is hard to copy quickly; the threat is higher in industrial flat products. Substitutes matter mainly in industrial markets, where the filing cites lower-priced imports and substitute materials. Both forces protect margin in the engine-component segment and leave the alloy segment's industrial sales more exposed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high in structure and moderated in practice: a small number of engine and airframe makers dominate demand, but no customer exceeded 10% of sales, long-term agreements are in place with most of them, and some are subject to renewal, renegotiation or re-pricing. Supplier power is limited for most inputs, which are available from more than one supplier, but nickel, titanium sponge, cobalt and ferrochromium come mostly from foreign sources that may face unstable conditions, and some supply arrangements rely on a limited number of suppliers, so supply or price shocks reach margin before surcharges reset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material: international sales were about 42% of FY2025 sales, 37% of 9M 2026 sales against 42% a year earlier, and the annual report says changes in trade policy could raise the cost of imported raw materials such as nickel and titanium sponge and of exported products. Economic factors are the main driver, through the commercial aerospace and industrial cycles described above. Technological change matters in that a new nickel-based superalloy entering production already dilutes the engine-component margin. Social factors matter through labour terms, with about 35% of the workforce under collective agreements, but they are not a primary credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are leverage that has fallen to 1.92x total and 1.46x net on reported EBITDA, liquidity that covers the next senior note maturity 3.11 times, and contracts and orders that cover about a year. Weaknesses are shareholder returns above free cash flow, concentration in aerospace and defense, and USD 203.0 million of funding outside reported debt. Opportunities are the growth in commercial jet engine and defense demand reflected in a USD 4.3 billion backlog, and capacity projects that can lift volume without new debt if funded from cash flow. Threats are a cut in engine build rates, trade-policy and input cost shocks that arrive before surcharges, and buybacks funded by borrowing.

fields.value: Free cash flow stability is Average: free cash flow was USD 168.1 million in FY2024, USD 333.7 million in FY2025 and USD 198.0 million in 9M 2026, with working capital swings and returns above it. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Strong on timing, because the 2033 notes were placed in 2026 and no senior note matures before FY2029, with ratings and market prices not supplied. Claims outside debt are modest against earnings: pension and retiree benefit liabilities were USD 187.9 million and environmental reserves about USD 15 million, with up to USD 21 million more reasonably possible. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next year or two the tailwinds are the order book of about USD 4.3 billion, price and mix gains, defense and specialty energy growth in the alloy segment, and a refinancing that has removed nearby maturities; these support revenue, margin and cash-flow visibility. The headwinds are superalloy ramp costs, inventory build, tariff and input cost exposure and payouts above free cash flow, which pressure margin, free cash flow and deleveraging. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether the earnings step-up lasts through the FY2029 and FY2030 maturities of USD 325.0 million of senior notes and USD 633.4 million in the largest ladder year, and on whether the company keeps returns within free cash flow as capacity growth ends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with a cut in commercial engine build rates or a trade shock that raises nickel and titanium costs ahead of surcharges. The first operating break is lower engine-component volume and a margin squeeze from fixed labour and superalloy ramp costs, with inventories, already up USD 255.1 million in 9M 2026, slow to unwind. Because EBITDA grew 22.75% on revenue growth of 9.29%, a reversal would cut EBITDA faster than revenue: at the FY2025 level of USD 789.0 million, with debt unchanged, total debt over EBITDA would be 2.35x and net debt 1.79x, and at the FY2024 level of USD 745.8 million, 2.49x and 1.90x. Cash flow would fall with EBITDA, and if buybacks continued free cash flow would again sit below returns. Management can slow growth capex, stop buybacks, which are discretionary, and release inventory. Liquidity of USD 1,012.3 million would still cover the USD 325.0 million FY2029 maturity 3.11 times, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but leverage would return to the levels of FY2024 and FY2025 and refinancing in FY2029 and FY2030 would be harder if the market had turned. The signals to watch are orders, the Adjusted EBITDA margin, free cash flow against returns and availability under the revolver.
